thread.title: Bears Win As Techs Weigh, But These 4 Top Stocks Defy Sell-Off | Investor's Business Daily

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Bears Win As Techs Weigh, But These 4 Top Stocks Defy Sell-Off | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks ended decisively lower after searching for direction through much of the session. The Nasdaq composite fell the hardest as tech stocks remained under pressure.
X The tech-heavy Nasdaq shed 0.9% as it continues to hit resistance at its 200-day moving average. The S&P 500, also meeting resistance at the 200-day line, fell 0.6%. Blue chips fared a bit better as the Dow Jones industrial average gave up 0.4%.
Small caps outperformed in the stock market today , with the Russell 2000 rallying 0.5% for its first decent gain since Oct. 3. Volume was lower on both the NYSE and Nasdaq, according to preliminary data.
Big-cap techs underperformed on the Dow as Cisco ( CSCO ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) each fell 2% or more. Cisco is holding support at its 200-day moving average and is 9% off its high. Microsoft is trading below its 50-day but remains 8% above its 200-day line.
Apple, an IBD 50 stock, continues to trade mostly between 215 and 234 as it tests support at the 50-day line. The iPhone maker could set up a chance to buy or add shares if it stages a solid rebound off the 50-day average (or 10-week on a weekly chart). However, all purchases are highly risky when the market is in correction.
Walgreens Boots Alliance ( WBA ), Procter & Gamble ( PG ) and Walt Disney ( DIS ) were among the Dow's biggest gainers. They rose 1.7%, 1.4% and 0.8%, respectively.
Retail Sales Slip, But Not These Top Stocks Despite lower-than-expected September retail sales , many retail industry groups advanced. Sales climbed 0.1% vs. economists' forecast for a 0.6% rise. Excluding autos, sales dipped 0.1% vs. views for a 0.4% increase. Specialty, discount, auto parts and supermarkets scored gains. In the discount space, Ollie's Bargain Outlet ( OLLI ) rose more than 1% as it moves up from the 50-day line. The stock was featured in today's Stock Spotlight column.
O'Reilly Automotive ( ORLY ) also added 1%. The auto parts retailer could set up a buy opportunity as it moves up from its 50-day line. It is also shaping a flat base with a potential buy point at 351.75. O'Reilly is one of the top stocks (99 Composite Rating) in the top-ranked auto parts group .

Shares are now nearly 30% extended from a 55.96 flat-base buy point cleared in early August, so investors could take some profits here. The stock also is rising from support at the 10-week line.
The chicken wings chain said it will announce Q3 results on Oct. 29. Analysts expect earnings to grow 12% to 19 cents a share on a 46% sales jump to $37.9 million. The IBD 50 stock has posted double-digit profit and sales growth for at least the past 18 quarters.
Nine Energy Service ( NINE ) surged 8%, at one point climbing past a 39.35 cup-base buy point during the session. Volume spiked five times higher than usual. The oilfield services provider has rallied 67% from its Jan. 19 offering price. It's thinly traded, with an average daily volume of about 206,000 shares. Nine Energy is acquiring Magnum Oil Tools International, a technology provider for the global oil and gas industry. Nine Energy is paying $493 million in cash and stock, plus contingency payments.
Telecom and solar were also among the day's top sector gainers, while some oil, steel and software stocks lagged.
